question: Which of the following displacement reactions is NOT possible ?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Cu(s) + PbCl2(aq) → CuCl2(aq) + Pb(s).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** displacement reaction** occurs when a more reactive element displaces a **less reactive element** from its compound.
 
• Cu(s) + PbCl2(aq) → CuCl2(aq) + Pb(s) is** not possible** because copper is less reactive than lead, so it **cannot displace** lead from its compound.
 
• In Pb(s) + CuCl2(aq) → PbCl2(aq) + Cu(s), lead is **more reactive **than copper, so it displaces copper from its compound.
 
• In Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s), iron is** more reactive** than copper, so it displaces copper from its compound.
 
• In Zn(s) + CuSO4(aq) → ZnSO4(aq) + Cu(s), zinc is **more reactive** than copper, so it displaces copper from its compound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Copper** is a **moderately reactive metal** that is commonly used in **electrical wiring, plumbing, and construction** materials.

 
 
• It is also an essential nutrient for **plants and animals.**
 
 
 
• **Lead** is a** highly toxic metal **that can cause serious health problems, including brain damage, kidney damage, and developmental delays.
 
 
• It is commonly found in **old paint, plumbing, and soil.**
 
 
 
• **Iron** is the most significant metal, but it** rusts easily,** making it a mysterious material.
 
 
• The majority is utilized in the **production of steel, in manufacturing, **and in civil engineering (reinforced concrete, girders, etc.).
 
 
 
• **Rubber, medications, and metal goods** are among the things that employ **zinc**.
 
 
• Roughly 75% of the zinc that is used is used as metal, primarily in the form of rolled zinc, zinc-based die casting alloy, alloying metal for making bronze and brass, and a** coating** to prevent iron and steel from corroding.
